title: Sequence-length drift-aware kernel chaining and low-cost probe policy
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: We observe that long-running services for chat and summarization experience gradual shifts in incoming sequence-length distributions ("sequence-length drift"). Static kernel picks tuned to historical medians produce suboptimal tail latency or cost when drift occurs.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, low-overhead kernel chaining mechanism that (1) detects short-term seqlen distribution shifts, (2) issues a constrained probe budget to validate alternative kernels, and (3) transparently chains execution to a more appropriate kernel for subsequent requests without violating latency SLOs. The system should work for both prefill-heavy and decode-heavy workloads and integrate with the runtime cost model.

Design overview:
- Signals and detection: use rolling 1, 5, and 15 minute seqlen histograms (token counts) per route + per-model. A simple EWMA-based drift score flags deviations from baseline.
- Probe budget: when drift score exceeds a threshold, schedule micro-probes on a tiny percentage of requests (0.5% by default). Probes execute an alternate kernel for a short path (prefill only or first N decode steps) to collect latency/throughput samples. Probes must be non-blocking and have a strict resource tag so they cannot evict production batch slots.
- Chaining policy: if probe results show >10% tail-latency improvement or >12% cost improvement with ≤1% accuracy variance for structured outputs, promote the kernel for the route. Promotion is done via a rollout window (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with canary telemetry. Rollback triggers on regression.
- Prefill vs decode: prioritize prefills for kernel selection since prefill costs dominate many workloads; however, for streaming-first customers we also evaluate decode-stage kernels using the probe-first-N approach to capture KV cache and autoregressive behavior.
- Warm-start and fingerprinting: maintain lightweight per-arch microbench fingerprints (exec time per token bucket) keyed by (model, arch, quantization, seqlen-bucket). Use these to seed the probe choices (avoid trying obviously incompatible kernels).
- Safety and SLOs: probes are rate-limited and preemptible. A safety gate prevents any new kernel from serving >20% of live traffic until post-canary KPIs (99th pct latency, error rate, model-output consistency) are stable for 30 minutes.
- Observability: add per-route telemetry: probe pass/fail, seqlen-histogram, promotion events, rollback reason, and cost-delta estimates. Hook into Console rollout dashboards.

Experiment plan:
- Phase A (lab): unit tests + microbench harness across representative GPUs (A100, H100, RTX-8k) and quantizations. Verify fingerprint warm-start reduces probe budget by 40% in simulation.
- Phase B (canary): enable on internal non-critical route (chat-internal-qa) at 0.5% traffic. Run 72-hour sweep with synthetic seqlen drift patterns.
- Phase C (customer pilot): opt-in with 3 customers; compare cost & latency vs control for 2 weeks.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runtime/kernel-chaining-seqlen-drift (draft)
- Perf harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-probes/tree/feature/seqlen-chaining
- Initial canary PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1837
- Dashboard prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/kernel-chaining-canary

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Probe frequency vs detection sensitivity: lower probe frequency reduces noise but increases time-to-adapt. We'll expose probe_budget as a per-customer knob.
- How to measure "output quality parity" for complex structured outputs — initial heuristic: task-specific checksums and embedding-distance thresholds. This will need PM/research input.
- Interactions with autoscaler: promoted kernels with higher memory use should trigger different scaling policies. Work with infra autoscale owners to add a kernel-memory hint on the node allocator.

Next steps (short-term):
1) Land fingerprint storage and retrieval (ENG-42190 dependency).
2) Implement drift detector and low-cost probe runner in the runtime (this ticket).
3) Add telemetry schema and Console widgets for canarying.

Success metrics:
- Reduce 95th pct latency regressions due to seqlen drift by >=40% on pilot routes.
- Net per-token cost decrease >=8% in pilot within 14 days of promotion.
- No increase in user-visible error rate >0.5%.
